decisions: THE DIRECTION OF A DEDUPE IS DECIDED BY CONSUMERS, NOT PREFERENCE. lib/commission.ts's monthKeyOf had 0 internal uses and 4 external consumers; lib/commission-rows.ts's had 2 internal and 0 external (ts-prune: 'exported but used in module'). So the copy nothing imported was DELETED and commission-rows imports the one everything already used. ts-prune no longer reports it as module-local, which is the check that it is genuinely shared now.

A DEDUPE'S SAFETY CLAIM MUST BE PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. The deleted body and the surviving body were diffed and are byte-identical (return iso.slice(0, 7)), so behaviour cannot change. Stating 'they were the same' without the diff is how a subtle difference ships.

THE LEAF PROPERTY OF lib/commission-rows.ts IS LOAD-BEARING and was the only real risk in adding an import to it. scripts/commission-rows-check.ts runs that module directly under node, so a runtime dependency breaks the money harness. lib/commission's only import is a TYPE (erased) and lib/db-types imports nothing at all - verified by RUNNING the script, not by reading imports.

monthKeyOf AND currentMonthKey ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND MUST NOT BE MERGED. monthKeyOf buckets a STORED ISO timestamp by its UTC instant, deliberately, so payroll grouping is deterministic across machines (lib/commission.ts). currentMonthKey answers which month the USER is in now, on the local clock (lib/utils.ts, beside todayKey). They agree for 21 hours a day, which is exactly why passing new Date().toISOString() into monthKeyOf survived so long as a way to get 'this month'.

THE COLUMN TYPE ON THE OTHER SIDE DECIDES WHETHER A MONTH COMPARISON IS CLEAN. trips.trip_date and customer_topups.topup_date are DATE (already a local calendar month); trips.delivered_at is TIMESTAMPTZ (bucketed by UTC by design). BreakdownReport and FinanceTab touch only DATE columns and now align exactly; CustomersTab touches both and keeps the stated residual above.

A MODULE-LEVEL CONST THAT READS THE CLOCK IS A BUG, NOT A CACHE. The original CURRENT_MONTH_KEY was computed once at module load and never rolled over - stale for the lifetime of a session or process. The UTC skew was the smaller half. Anything answering 'what is now' must be called, not captured.

MONTH_KEY IS LOAD-BEARING ON THE WRITE PATH. v_commissions_monthly attributes specials, adjustments AND the bonus by exact string match, and v_driver_payslip_basis reads through it. The 'month_key is kept only as a human label' comment on setCommissionBonus describes that upsert's CONFLICT TARGET (driver_id alone) and is not a statement about the views.

MIGRATIONS ARE COMMITTED THE MOMENT THE APPLY IS CONFIRMED (the db-reset rule), and the apply is VERIFIED rather than taken on report. 0120's anon check was the one that mattered: default privileges re-grant anon on every newly created relation and a REVOKE does not survive a DROP. It held - 40 views, 40 invoker, 0 anon-readable.
